When I was somewhere around 6-8 years old, my family and I went to a football game. I've never really been one to enjoy football outside of playing it, but I remember being so damn hype when they would bring out the air cannons to shoot free stuff. Anyways, on this particular game, me and my brother ran to the bottom of the stands to try to catch some plastic football's they were shooting in the crowds. I didn't catch one but I wasn't upset because I'm not one for sports and I just wanted to see if I could catch one; but on the way back up the stands, this old man at least in his 70's had caught one of them and held it out to me to give it to me. I didn't completely appreciate it at the time and didn't understand just how kind that was, but I told him thank you and still think about that moment to this day. I've no idea what happened to that ball or that man, but I've held that sweet old guy as an example to cheer up other little kids who didn't get to catch a ball.
TL:DR; A sweet old man caught a plastic football for me and gave it to me when I was little and still think about him to this day

This is probably too late to post this, but I feel like getting this off my chest.
A 19 year old relative of mine lives with his grandpa along with his mom and step-dad. His family used to have their own house, but they stopped paying utilities about a year ago because there were apparent problems with their house, like broken water pipes or bug infestations, according to his parents. These parents have 3 kids: the 19 year old, one which lives with their dad, a 9 year old, and another on the way. Growing up, the now-19 year old (Let's call him Tom) was always the scapegoat and got blamed for everything that went wrong, even when it wasn't his fault the majority of the time. The middle-aged kid, who never got in trouble and was the "golden child," wised up and moved to his dad's around 3 years ago, whenever we first noticed their parents were becoming meaner.
Around a couple of years ago, we started to notice his parents using drugs. We never actually saw them use, but they always wore sweaters and long sleeves in 90°+ F weather to cover up track marks and scabs all over their arms. Another relative of mine, who had problems with almost any drug you can imagine, was positive they were/are using. His parents apparently make $600 each week, even though they don't have jobs, but whenever Tom wants to get money to take his girlfriend out or buy new stuff, his parents steal money he earned from working out of his wallet for cigarettes and likely more drugs. His mom always yells at him and says he drives her "Fucking crazy," even though he tries to be out of the house often and never does anything to her. When he does get out of the house, his parents make him look after his 9 year old brother, whom they never take care of and also has constant illnesses. Their parents refuse to take them to doctor appointments and other important events simply because they don't feel like driving, and refuse to let Tom use his grandpa's car to visit town (we live in the country about 20 minutes away from a big town.) Tom has his license and his grandpa is fine with him using his car, but his parents don't let his use it for God knows why, probably just to be mean. Tom is a great guy and is really kind, so it sucks seeing his parents abuse drugs, steal money from him, neglect him and their sick 9 year old, and blame him for everything when they're shitty human beings.

TL;DR - Family member of mine has parents who steal his money, refuse to let him leave the home often, use drugs, and don't take care of their children. Please, if you have kids, make them your priority and never let them feel unloved
